title: Admin Action Custody Flow: Data Residency Locking, Retention Policies, and Append-Only Exporter
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Deliver an append-only export pipeline and residency-aware custody flow for admin actions (config changes, role grants, access revocations). This ticket covers: (1) a write-once exporter that pushes signed batches into region-scoped WORM buckets, (2) manifest generation with cryptographic custody stamps and retention markers, and (3) an automated evidence report that exports compliance-ready bundles for legal/forensic requests. Goal: ensure tamper-evident admin audit data with programmable retention and easy handoff for auditors.
acceptance_criteria: All admin action events are written to the append-only exporter within 10s of occurrence for host-region traffic
Exporter writes manifest + event bundle to region-scoped WORM store with object ACLs and retention metadata
Each exported bundle includes a signed manifest (HSM-backed key) and a Merkle root of events
Retention policy tags are applied and honored by the storage lifecycle (retain, legal-hold, purge)
Automated evidence report generator can produce a compressed, signed bundle and S3 presigned URL for auditors
End-to-end test demonstrating tamper detection: modified bundle must fail signature/merkle validation in verification job
technical_design: Architecture: exporter service runs in control-plane and data-plane modes. Control-plane coordinates residency tagging and retention rules; data-plane handles event batching, local persist, HSM-signing, and cross-region replication for customer-configured residency policies. Bundles are emitted with a compact manifest: {region_tag, start_ts, end_ts, event_count, merkle_root, retention_label, signature}. The exporter writes to a write-once storage path (WORM-enabled buckets or object-store with retention lock). A verification worker consumes stored bundles, validates signatures and merkle roots, and indexes verification outcomes into the Console for SRE/Compliance. Key management uses customer-managed KMS where available; fallback to Redwood HSM with audit trail. Edge cases: network partitions, partial writes — exporter writes a .tmp then atomically renames to final path after successful sign/flush.
implementation_notes: Create exporter binary with 2 modes: immediate-flush (low-latency) and periodic-batch (cost-optimized)
Integrate with event-sourcing stream (admin-events topic) and add idempotent checkpointing
Use our existing HSM wrapper (kms-signer) for manifest signing; add support for customer KMS alias override
Write final bundles to region-specific WORM prefix: /custody/{customer}/{region}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/bundle-{seq}.pb
Emit verification metadata to console: bundle_id, signed_by, signed_at, verification_status
Add retention/hold API hooks so Console/Policy engine can set legal_hold:true on bundle prefixes
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff. Alignment with Compliance and Legal on minimum evidence fields. Decided manifest must include signer key id and merkle_root for compact verification.
2026-03-04: Prototype exporter that batches 5m windows and emits ndjson bundles to local test store. Verified merkle root computation against reference vector.
2026-03-08: Integration demo with staging KMS. Discovered permission gap for write-lock on S3 retention configuration; opened infra follow-up with infra-ops.
2026-03-12: Implemented atomic .tmp->final rename flow. Added initial Console hooks to display bundle IDs and retention labels.
2026-03-14: PR opened for exporter core and verification worker (see PRs below). Began load test for 1k admin events/sec burst pattern.
review_feedback: Security review (2026-03-10): Ensure signer key rotation is possible without breaking verification of historical bundles; agreed to include key-id in manifest and maintain key history index
Compliance (2026-03-11): Request to include original event timestamps and canonicalization format; action: add RFC3339 timestamps and deterministic event JSON ordering
SRE (2026-03-13): Suggest backpressure path if WORM-store throttles; design decision: queue to local SSD with retention policy and alerting for prolonged backpressure

rollout_plan: Phase 1: launch in staging (single region) with immediate-flush mode and Redwood-managed KMS for internal accounts. Phase 2: opt-in alpha for customers with residency or KMS requirements (add region tagging and customer KMS). Phase 3: mandatory retention enforcement by runtime; expose Console controls for legal hold and export-on-demand. Rollout gated by successful verification worker run on 30 days of bundles and passing security review.
qa_plan: Unit tests: manifest consistency, merkle computation, signature verification
Integration: end-to-end export -> write to WORM -> verification worker marks verified
Fault injection: simulate partial write and network drop, ensure bundle not visible until fully written
Compliance scenario: generate legal_hold flag and ensure bundle persists beyond retention expiry
monitoring_playbook: Create Grafana dashboard with metrics: exporter.event_rate, exporter.batch_latency, exporter.write_errors, verification.success_rate, retention.lock_errors. Alert if verification.success_rate < 99.9% over 1h or if write_errors spike > 0.5% of events. Run weekly audit job that verifies a random sample of bundles and stores results in the compliance index.
unresolved_risks: Customer-managed KMS introduces key-availability risk: if customer revokes keys, historical verification could break; mitigation: require export of public key material to Redwood verification index at onboarding
Cross-region replication for residency-restricted customers may conflict with policy — need policy-aware routing and legal signoff
Retention enforcement in third-party object stores has subtle semantics across clouds; test matrix required for S3, GCS, Azure Blob
